pr_title: Detect Homebrew on Mac M1 (Apple Silicon)
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
The `ansible_pkg_mgr` fact is `unknown` on Macs with M1 chip (Apple Silicon -- ARM architecture).

The root cause is that Homebrew's default install path on ARM is `/opt/homebrew`.

Fixes #73887
Closes #73896

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
facts

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

Homebrew's default install location for macOS on ARM is `/opt/homebrew`. Source: https://docs.brew.sh/FAQ.

On a Mac M1 (Apple Silicon), homebrew will be installed at `/opt/homebrew/bin/brew`.

Without this fix, the `ansible_pkg_mgr` fact will be `unknown`.

```
❯ ansible localhost -m setup | grep "ansible_pkg_mgr"
[WARNING]: No inventory was parsed, only implicit localhost is available
        "ansible_pkg_mgr": "unknown",
```

With the fix, the value will be `homebrew`:

```
❯ ansible localhost -m setup | grep "ansible_pkg_mgr"
[WARNING]: No inventory was parsed, only implicit localhost is available
        "ansible_pkg_mgr": "homebrew",
```
pr_comments: @samdoran Thanks for accepting the PR. I'll create the backports.

issue_context.title: fact gathering does not auto-detect homebrew on Mac with M1
issue_context.body:
### Summary

module_utils/facts/system/pkg_mgr.py does not detect homebrew on Mac with M1.

homebrew on Mac with M1 is installed to /opt/homebrew/bin/brew.
But, module_utils/facts/system/pkg_mgr.py only search '/usr/local/bin/brew'.

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

facts

### Ansible Version

```console (paste below)
$ ansible --version
ansible 2.9.6
  config file = /etc/ansible/ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['/home/kimata/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/ansible
  executable location = /usr/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.8.5 (default, Jan 27 2021, 15:41:15) [GCC 9.3.0]
```


### Configuration

```console (paste below)
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed

```


### OS / Environment

Ubuntu 20.04.2 LTS

### Steps to Reproduce

<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->
```console (paste below)
$ ansible macbook -m setup
```


### Expected Results

"ansible_pkg_mgr": "homebrew",



### Actual Results

<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->
```console (paste below)
$ ssh macbook brew --prefix
/opt/homebrew

$ ansible macbook -m setup
(snip)
        "ansible_machine": "arm64",
        "ansible_memfree_mb": 6712,
        "ansible_memtotal_mb": 8192,
        "ansible_model": "MacBookAir10,1",
        "ansible_nodename": "macbook.green-rabbit.net",
        "ansible_os_family": "Darwin",
        "ansible_osrevision": "199506",
        "ansible_osversion": "20D91",
        "ansible_pkg_mgr": "unknown",  <---
        "ansible_processor": "Apple M1",
        "ansible_processor_cores": "8",
        "ansible_processor_vcpus": "8",
        "ansible_product_name": "MacBookAir10,1",
```

Until #73896 is merged, I was able to work around this with:

```
- name: Set pkg_mgr for macOS
  when: ansible_facts['distribution'] == 'MacOSX'
  set_fact:
    pkg_mgr: homebrew
    cacheable: yes
```

review_comments: I don't think the `lambda` is necessary here. You should be able to set [`return_value`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.mock.html#unittest.mock.Mock.return_value) instead.
@samdoran Thanks for reviewing. How would you set `return_value` to be `True` only for that specific path and not for the others?

Oh, I misread this. I thought it was returning the path not the result of an evaluation. I tend to try and avoid `lambda` at all costs (harder to read/maintain usually), but I don't see a better way to write the test.
Makes sense, thanks for checking. I thought this was the most concise way to do it.
